causal_diagnosis: The policy learned to do nothing (action 0, 93%) because the dense distance penalty (-2 * distance) dominates the reward, making any movement costly. The crash penalty (-100) applies to all terminations, including timeouts, so the agent is punished equally for failing early or trying longer. The success bonus (100) is never reached because the condition is too strict (requires near-pad, low speeds, small angle) and the agent never gets close enough. The main engine (action 2) is never used because it incurs a fuel penalty without any compensating benefit, and the distance penalty makes moving toward the pad unattractive.
component_interaction_diagnosis: The distance shaping (-2 * distance) is the dominant component by absolute return (-142.7), but it is always negative, so the agent minimizes it by staying near the starting position (which is far from pad). The crash penalty (-100) is applied on every termination, making all episodes equally bad. The success bonus (0.0) never fires. The fuel penalty (-0.03 per main engine use) further discourages using action 2. The time penalty (-0.1 per step) is small but adds up over ~72 steps. The net effect is that the agent receives a large negative reward regardless of behavior, so it defaults to the cheapest action (no-op).
action_coverage_diagnosis: Action 2 (main engine) is unused. This action is necessary for controlled descent and hovering. The current reward makes it unattractive because: (1) it incurs a fuel penalty, (2) it moves the lander, increasing the distance penalty, and (3) there is no positive incentive to use it. The other actions (0, 1, 3) are used but only action 0 dominates. The policy has not learned to use the main engine to approach the pad.

The trajectory phase report shows failure_phase='action_coverage_incomplete' because action 2 is unused. The objective signal alignment audit shows success_like_terminal_rate=0.0, meaning the reward's success signal is never triggered.
